BOPEN.heard: Building virtual environments exam prep, key terms, blender to go-dough. 30 terms for getting a model out of blender and into a go-dough game, then proving it arrived at the right size, the right way up, and with collision that works.

BIDEA.heard: Hollow, this is Liam in for bear. Newcomers see a prop standing at the right height and go-dough and assume all is well. But a model can look right and still be a two meter cube wearing a scale and anything built from that mesh inherits it. Looking right is only a claim. This film goes through the terms each one shown, so you know what to measure.

BDEFS.heard: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow. In the book text, the course text uses and explains the term. In the glossary, the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it. Video only, the term comes from a video lecture and is not in the course text or on the term list. Computed, the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs. Illustrative data, numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured. Conceptual, a drawing of the idea with no data behind it.

B0101.heard: This table is the map, 30 terms and four groups, all about getting a model from Blender into GoDo and proving it arrived intact. First, driving Blender, MCP the model context protocol, MCP tool, MCP server and add-on, Bpy, headless Blender and the Python exit code flag.

B0102.heard: The second group is units, axes, and transforms. Unit, unit, scale, up-axis, axis conversion, apply transforms, node scale, and origin and pivot. These terms explain why a model arrives lying down or the wrong size.

B0103.heard: The third group is export, import, and collision. GLTF, GLB, material through export, import file, name suffix, collision shape, and convex and concave. These terms say how a model and its collider reach Godot.

B0104.heard: The fourth group is measuring in budget. Dimensions, bounding box, claim versus measurement, triangle count, high poly and low poly, texture baking, LOD, which means level of detail, script as source, version control, and naming conventions. How you prove the result, keep it cheap and repeat it.

B0201.heard: Three boxes, a coding agent, an MCP server, and Blender with an add-on. MCP is a standard way for an AI app to call tools inside another program. The agent sends a request, and Blender runs it and sends back a result. Both sides follow one agreed set of message rules, unlike the script route, MCP works on a live Blender window. For example, an agent asks a running Blender for the size of a crate you just modeled, and gets the numbers back.

B0202.heard: An MCP tool is one named action the agent is allowed to call with typed arguments. The list shows four tools the server offers. Get scene info, get object info, execute blender code in red which runs python inside blender and export scene which writes a model file. For example, to check a barrel prop, the agent calls get object info with the barrel's name as its argument and reads back the barrel's size and position.

B0203.heard: The MCP server and add-on are the two halves of the connection. The server is a small relay program that the agent starts. The add-on runs inside Blender and receives the calls over a local socket. That socket has no login and no encryption, so keep the port on local host. For example, before an agent shapes rocks for your level in Blender, you enable the add-on inside Blender, start it, and register the server with your coding agent.

B0301.heard: A short script with an export line at the bottom. BPY is Blender's Python module, the set of commands that control Blender. A script calls it directly and the MCP tools call the same module underneath. Here the script adds a cube, scales it into a column and exports it. For example, an agent can write a BPY script that builds a low polycoin, gives it a named gold material and exports it, so the coin can be rebuilt anytime.

B0302.heard: Headless Blender means running Blender with no window from the command line. It is also called Background Mode. The B flag runs it in the background, the factory startup flag skips your own startup file, and the Python flag runs the script. Nobody has to watch a screen. For example, after you change one measurement in your build script, an agent runs Blender Headless to rebuild every fence prop in the level, then reads the printed sizes.

B0303.heard: The same broken script run two ways. The Python exit code flag typed with two dashes in front makes a script error and blender with exit code one which means failure. Without it in the top box the error is printed and the run still exits zero which looks like success. For example if the build script for a tree prop has a typo, the flag makes your automated check stop and report it, instead of carrying on as if the tree was built.

B0401.heard: A ruler and meters with the robot capsule in the post beside it. The unit is the length one coordinate step stands for, usually a meter. Blender GLTF and Godot all treat one unit as one meter. The robot capsule is 2.1 meters tall and the post is 1.8. For example, when you model a legend blender, its height in units is its height in meters and Godot, so you can tell whether the robot can climb onto it.

B0402.heard: Unit scale is the factor that turns blender units into meters. A mesh 1.8 units tall is 1.8 meters at unit scale 1.0, but 1.8 centimeters at 0.01. A unit is the length of a step and unit scale is the multiplier on it. For example, a sword built in a scene with the wrong unit scale arrives in the player's hand far too small to see.

B0403.heard: Two sets of axes, blender on the left and go-dough on the right. The up axis is the axis that points up. Blender is Z up and GLTF and go-dough are Y up. Go-dough's forward direction is minus Z. Both systems are right-handed. For example, in go-dough a script that lifts a moving platform toward the ceiling raises the platform's Y position, not at Z, because Y is the up axis there.

B0404.heard: Axis conversion is the step that turns one up axis into the other. The exporters plus y-up option rotates the model a quarter turn about x, the matrix shown, so Blender Z-extent becomes Godot's y. The columns box was 0.2, 0.2, 1.8, and Blender, and in Godot the 1.8 sits on y. For example, a lamp post exported with that option switched off arrives and the level lying on its side.

B0501.heard: A column with its numbers, apply transforms means baking position, rotation and scale into the mesh, then resetting them to neutral. The column began as a 2 meter cube wearing a scale. After apply the mesh data is 0.2 by 1.8 by 0.2 and the object scale is 1. The drawn size never changed. For example, after squashing a box into a flat platform, you apply scale so its collider is built at its real size.

B0502.heard: Node scale is a scale left on the node instead of baked into the mesh. Here a ball is squashed by a node scale of 1 by 0.4, but its sphere collider has only one radius, so it sticks out 0.6 meters above and below. A scale left on the node reaches everything built from the mesh. For example, a boulder flattened in blender without applying scale keeps that scale on its node, so a sphere collider leaves the player bumping into air above it.

B0503.heard: Two posts on a floor line each with a red dot. The origin is the point and objects position and rotation are measured from. The pivot is the point it rotates and scales around. The left post stands because its origin is at the base. The right post has its origin at the center, so it sinks 0.9 meters into the floor. For example, a door's pivot belongs on its hinge edge, so it swings open instead of spinning around its middle.

B0601.heard: Code on the left in two bars. Dimensions are an object size and meters on each axis, as Blender reports it. Here a script sets the scale and prints the dimensions at once and gets 2-2-2, which is stale. After the scene refreshes, it prints 0.2, 0.2, 1.8, which is fresh. For example, if an agent reports a crate's dimensions straight after scaling it, those numbers may be the old size, so ask again after the update.

B0602.heard: A dashed box grows around the post's corner points. A bounding box is the smallest axis aligned box that holds an object. It is the minimum and maximum of the vertices, nothing else. Here 12 points give a box 0.78 wide because of the pennant and 1.8 tall. It's half sizes are called the extents. For example, to check their new treasure chest fits through a doorway in your level, a test can compare the chest's bounding box with the gap.

B0603.heard: Three builds of the same column each claim to be 0.2 by 1.8 by 0.2 meters. A claim is what a name or a script says. A measurement is what a test reads from the file. Only the good build passes. No Y-up lies on its side and no apply carries a scale. For example, a model file named SmallRock is only a claim, and a test that reads its size from the file is the measurement.

B0701.heard: A list of the files one export writes, GLTF is an open 3D format and the preferred way to move models into game engines. Its text form writes a readable scene file with nodes, meshes and materials, a separate binary file of vertex data and loose texture images, three kinds of file to keep together. For example, export a treasure chest as text GLTF when you want get to show what changed in its scene each time you edit it.

B0702.heard: Now the same piece is packed into one file. GLB is GLTF packed into a single binary file with the scene, the vertex data, and the images together. GLTF keeps the scene as text with separate data beside it, and GLB puts everything inside one file. For example, a small prop such as a key the player picks up is easiest to ship as one GLB file, with no loose textures to lose.

B0703.heard: Three columns, blender, GLTF and Godot. Material through export means a named blender material arrives in Godot under the same name. Postmetal and flag cloth each cross and become a standard material 3D, and the resource name is still postmetal, so a test can check it. A blender only node does not cross. For example, name your lava material in blender. And a Godot test can confirm the lava floor, still carries that exact material name after import.

B0704.heard: Settings lines from a real file. The import file, the one ending in dot import, is the text file Godot keeps beside each imported model, and its settings decide what Godot builds. The red line use node type suffixes is false in the Walker platformer demos models while a fresh import sets it true. Copy the demos file and Godot ignores your name hints, for example if a new enemy model arrives without its collider. Open its import file and check that line first.

B0801.heard: A table of endings for mesh names. A name suffix is a tail on a mesh's name that tells Godot what to build. Dash call adds concave collision, dash conf call adds convex collision, and dash conf call only removes the mesh and makes a convex body. With the suffix setting on, you get a static body 3D. With it off, a visible box and no collision. For example, name a box around a fence dash conf call only. And Godot makes it the fence's invisible collider.

B0802.heard: The box collider becomes a tapered hull. A collision shape is the simple shape physics uses, not the detailed mesh you see. The pennant should stay outside it. In this drawings count, 52 of 1,066 pennant points are still inside the hull, and the goal is zero. A physics sampling of the real post found 572 for the box and 55 for the hull. For example, a tree gets a simple trunk-shaped collider. So the player walks under its leaves.

B0803.heard: Two shapes each with a line between two and side points. Convex means no dense, so a line between any two and side points stays inside. Concave means the shape has a hollow, so a line can leave it. Here 60% of the line leaves the concave shape and none leaves the convex one. Convex is cheap for physics, and concave is exact but costly. For example, a bowl the player can stand inside needs a concave collider, while a crate is convex.

B0901.heard: Four bars for one box, the post's base. Triangle count is the number of triangles in a mesh, and it is what engines budget buy. Blender shows faces in the GPU, the graphics processor splits vertices. In this example, the box has eight vertices, six faces, 12 triangles, and 24 GPU vertices, and the whole post is 42 triangles. For example, when a phone game allows each prop a fixed budget. You compare its triangle count with that budget, not the face count blender displays.

B0902.heard: Two bars on a log scale. High poly is a very detailed sculpt, and low poly is the cheap copy of it that the engine runs. In this made up example, the sculpt has two million triangles around number, and the low poly post has 42, about 47,619 times fewer. For example, an artist sculpts a dragon's head with every scale in detail, then builds a low poly version of that head for the game to draw.

B0903.heard: A wavy line becomes a flat one plus a strip of greys. Texture baking moves the fine detail of the sculpt into an image that the low poly mesh wears. In this drawing the high poly surface has 80 points, the low poly one has 2 and the baked image keeps the bumps as 20 values. The cheap mesh wears the expensive surface. For example, the carved runes on a stone door can be baked into its texture, so a flat low poly door still shows them.

B0904.heard: A step chart as the post moves away. LOD level of detail means cheaper versions of a model swapped in at a distance. In these illustrative levels, the post uses 42 triangles up close, 21 past 10 meters and 11 past 25. At 40 meters it is drawn with 11, where a level switches the mesh can visibly jump, which is called popping. For example, trees far down a road in an open level can use their cheapest version. Since nobody sees the missing branches.

B1001.heard: A script goes into headless blender and a model comes out. Script as source means the script that built the asset is what you commit, review and rerun, and the GLB is only its output. The script is the source and the GLB is the build product. Running the final script gave the same bytes and get showed no change. For example, if a plate ester finds a ramp too steep, you change one number in the ramps, build script and rebuild, not the exported file.

B1002.heard: The same edit in two kinds of file. Version control is software that records every version of a file and who changed it, and warns when two people's changes clash. On the left, the binary blender file only says the files differ. On the right, the script's diff shows the top of the poll moving from 1.7 to 1.8. For example, when two students edit the same level, version control shows who move the goal flag and warns of the clash.

B1003.heard: Four file names checked against one rule, the word prop, and underscore, then lower case words. Naming conventions are agreed rules for how files and objects are named. Two names pass. Post final new two and cube point zero zero three must be renamed. Godo's dash conf call only suffix is a naming convention two because the importer reads it, for example. A team that starts every enemy file name with the same prefix lets a script find and load all of them.

B1101.heard: These are look-alike pairs. Scale is a multiplier on the object here a 2 meter mesh times 0.9. Size is the real dimension in meters 1.8 measured, the same picture, two different numbers.

B1102.heard: The MCP route leaves a transcript of tool calls, get seen info, execute blender code, export seen and no file records how. The script route is a file you can diff and rerun, and a rerun gives the same GLB.

B1103.heard: The visual mesh is the detailed shape you see 42 triangles. The collision shape is the simple shape physics uses, 12 triangles, the dashed box around the post.

B1104.heard: Concave has a hollow so a line can leave it and 60% of this line is outside. Convex has no dents so a line stays inside with 0% outside.

B1201.heard: Vague requests were written as exact instructions. Make the prop the right size becomes keep unit scale at 1.0, apply scale, and requires 0.2 by 1.8 by 0.2 meters within 1 centimeter. Only one of three builds matches.

B1202.heard: It's lying on its side becomes export with plus Y up on, then check that Blender's Z extent shows up as GoDo's Y. In the chart, the 1.8 moves from the Z group to the Y group.

B1203.heard: Make the collision work becomes name a simple mesh collision dash conv call only and turn use node type suffixes on. With the setting true one collider, a static body 3D, with it false, a visible box and no collision.

B1204.heard: Keep it cheap becomes keep the post under 100 triangles. The visual mesh is 42 and the collider 12, so the post sits inside this illustrative budget.

B1205.heard: Keep the flag out of the collider, becomes sample the pennant on a 1 cm grid and requires zero points inside. The box had 572 of 1066 inside, the hull 52 by this drawings model rather than a physics test and the goal is zero.

B1301.heard: This is a checklist of six questions to ask before you trust an imported model. First is Unit Scale 1.0, so one unit is 1 meter.

B1302.heard: Second, did you apply rotation and scale, so every node scale is one. A scale left on a node reaches everything built from the mesh.

B1303.heard: Third is the model Y up in Godot with Blender Z on Godot's Y. If it is not, the model lies on its side.

B1304.heard: Fourth, do the measured dimensions match the claim within one centimeter. Read the numbers from the file, not from the name.

B1305.heard: Fifth is the collider a simple, separate mesh and did its suffix take effect. Look for a static body 3D, not a visible box.

B1306.heard: Sixth is the script committed and does a script error end the run non-zero. Then say it exactly. Not make it the right size, but 0.2 by 1.8 by 0.2 meters. Scale 1.

BVDT.heard: Let's recap, MCP drives a live Blender and a BPY script runs it headless. Add the Python Exit Code flag or a broken script Exit 0. Blender is Z up and the plus Y up option puts it Z on Godot's Y. Apply transforms so the scale lives in the mesh and not on the node. A name suffix builds collision only when the import setting is on. A name is a claim and only a number read from the file is evidence.

BHTF.heard: Quizme I'm moving a model from Blender into Go-Doh with short game-making cases one at a time. Use the terms Unit Scale Up Axis Apply Transforms, Node Scale, GLB, Name Suffix, Collision Shape, Convex, Triangle Count, and Claim Versus Measurement. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.

BOUT.heard: Key terms blender to go dough at Nick Bear Brown.
